LRC-CPPT: Multicenter randomized double-blind study with average 7.4 years follow-up. Treatment group received cholestyramine plus moderate cholesterol-lowering diet vs placebo plus same diet. Both groups followed the same moderate cholesterol-lowering diet. This is primarily a drug trial (cholestyramine), not testing dietary saturated fat reduction as the intervention. The diet was not the variable being tested.
Secondary analysis of LRC-CPPT results. Same issue as 163 - primarily a drug trial, not testing dietary saturated fat reduction as the intervention.

Controlled trial of combination low sodium, low fat, high fibre diet in treated hypertensive patients. Duration not specified but appears short-term. Multifactorial intervention. No mortality/CVD morbidity outcomes.
Factorial trial with 1 month and 6 month follow-ups. Does not meet 24-month minimum. Multifactorial intervention (booklet, salt, prompts for fruit/vegetable/fibre, low fat).
Sequential diet study comparing saturated vs polyunsaturated fatty acid-rich diets. Short-term study examining HDL metabolism. No mortality/CVD morbidity outcomes.
8 months follow-up (2 weeks + 6 months after rehabilitation). Does not meet 24-month minimum. Psychological intervention to reduce saturated fat intake post-MI. No mortality/CVD morbidity outcomes.

Lyon Diet Heart Study: Randomized secondary prevention trial with mean 27 months follow-up. Compared Mediterranean alpha-linolenic acid-rich diet (lower in saturated fat) vs usual prudent diet post-MI. Measured cardiac deaths and nonfatal MI. This meets criteria: randomized, reduced saturated fat, compared with higher sat fat/usual diet, not multifactorial, adult humans with CVD, >24 months, mortality/CVD morbidity data available.

Lyon Diet Heart Study methods paper describing bias control. Same trial as 169 - randomized secondary prevention trial with Mediterranean-type diet vs control. Mean follow-up extended to 46 months in final report. Measured major cardiac events including death and MI. Meets all criteria.

Lyon Diet Heart Study final report: Randomized secondary prevention trial with mean 46 months follow-up. Compared Mediterranean-type diet (lower in saturated fat) vs prudent Western-type diet post-MI. Measured cardiac death, nonfatal MI, and other cardiovascular events. Meets all criteria: randomized, reduced saturated fat, compared with higher sat fat/usual diet, not multifactorial, adult humans with CVD, >24 months, mortality/CVD morbidity data available.

Lyon Diet Heart Study analysis: Same randomized trial with mean 27 months follow-up. Mediterranean diet vs control diet in post-MI patients. Measured cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, and other cardiac events. Meets all criteria.

Lyon Diet Heart Study cancer analysis: Same randomized trial with 4 years follow-up. Mediterranean diet vs control diet in CHD patients. Measured total deaths, cardiac deaths, and cancer outcomes. Meets all criteria for CVD outcomes.

Lyon Diet Heart Study Cretan Mediterranean diet analysis: Randomized secondary prevention trial with mean 27 months follow-up. Compared Cretan Mediterranean diet (lower in saturated fat) vs usual prescribed diet post-MI. Measured recurrent MI, cardiovascular events, and cardiac/total death. Meets all criteria.
Small study (60 patients) of antiatherogenic diet with flavonoids. Duration not specified. No mortality/CVD morbidity outcomes - only clinical manifestations and lipid spectrum.
1-year randomized trial of evening primrose oil in women with breast cysts. Not a saturated fat reduction intervention. No CVD outcomes.

Fails multiple criteria: (1) Duration is only 6 weeks, failing criterion 6 (requires at least 24 months). (2) Patients are 24-48 hours post-AMI, constituting 'acutely ill' per criterion 5. Fails multiple criteria: (1) Duration is only 1 year follow-up, failing criterion 6 (requires at least 24 months). This study does target saturated fat reduction in adults with type 2 diabetes. However, duration is only 12 months (fails criterion 6 requiring ≥24 months). Additionally, outcomes focus on dietary fat targets achieved, not mortality or cardiovascular morbidity (fails criterion 7).

Randomized trial comparing low-fat (≤7% saturated fat) vs Mediterranean-style diet after first MI. Both diets targeted saturated fat reduction (meets criterion 2). Compared to usual care control (meets criterion 3). Single dietary intervention, not multifactorial (meets criterion 4). Adult post-MI patients (meets criterion 5). Median follow-up 46 months, range 18-72 months (meets criterion 6). Reports primary-outcome-free survival including all-cause/cardiac deaths, MI, heart failure, stroke (meets criterion 7).

TOHP Phase I examining sodium reduction intervention. Duration is 18 months (fails criterion 6). Intervention targets sodium, not saturated fat (fails criterion 2). Outcomes are blood pressure changes, not mortality/cardiovascular morbidity (fails criterion 7).

This is a recruitment methodology paper, not an intervention study reporting outcomes. It evaluates different approaches to participant enrollment. No intervention outcomes, no saturated fat reduction focus, no mortality or CVD morbidity data. Fails criteria 2, 6, and 7.

While the intervention includes a Mediterranean low-saturated fat diet, it is a multifactorial program (diet, stress management, exercise, group support, smoking cessation) - fails criterion 4 (not multifactorial). The intervention promotes eating patterns low in fat and high in fiber, but is not specifically focused on reducing saturated fat intake (fails criterion 2). This is a project description/feasibility study. The intervention provides general advice to reduce cardiovascular risk, not specifically targeting saturated fat reduction (fails criterion 2). While participants are being followed for 10 years on CVD morbidity and mortality, this paper reports only 1.5-year follow-up with cholesterol changes. While DASH meals include reduced saturated fat, the intervention duration is only 12 months (fails criterion 6: at least 24 months). Outcomes are dietary compliance measures (DASH accordance, saturated fat accordance) with no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity data (fails criterion 7).

The intervention is improved glucose control using pharmacologic therapies (sulfonylurea, insulin, metformin) vs conventional therapy, not saturated fat reduction (fails criterion 2). While the study has adequate duration (9 years) and reports cardiovascular complications, the intervention does not target dietary fat intake.

This study focuses on glucose control interventions (diet, tablets, insulin) in Type II diabetes, not on reducing saturated fat intake. The UKPDS compares different therapies for glycemic control, not dietary fat modifications. Does not meet criterion 2 (intention to reduce saturated fat).

While randomised and approximately 24 months duration, the study does not clearly state an intention to reduce saturated fat intake - it focuses on 'intensified diet education' for metabolic control. More importantly, there are no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes reported (criterion 7). Only metabolic control and lipid parameters are measured.

Randomised 2-year trial comparing low-carbohydrate vs low-fat diets. However, the primary focus is on carbohydrate content (20% vs 55-60% E%), not specifically on reducing saturated fat. More critically, there are no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes - only weight, HbA1c, and lipid parameters are reported. Does not meet criterion 7.

Duration is only 6 months, failing criterion 6 (minimum 24 months required). Additionally, outcomes are limited to inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-1Ra, IL-6, TNFR) with no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity data. The study compares low-carbohydrate vs low-fat diets focusing on inflammation, not specifically on saturated fat reduction.

This is a cross-sectional study examining psychosocial determinants (attitude, self-efficacy, habit, etc.) of intention to change fat consumption. It is NOT a randomised trial (fails criterion 1). The study uses logistic regression to predict intention, not to evaluate intervention effects on health outcomes.

Randomised 2-year trial where walnuts were added to diet, resulting in reduced SFA intake (displacement effect). However, the primary intervention was walnut supplementation, not intentional saturated fat reduction. More importantly, outcomes are limited to nutrient intake assessments - there are no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes (fails criterion 7).

Study population consists of adults on home haemodialysis, who are acutely ill with renal failure. This violates criterion 5 (excludes acutely ill patients). Additionally, outcomes are limited to serum lipoprotein levels with no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity data. The fat-modified diet targets cholesterol reduction with P/S ratio of 1.0, not specifically saturated fat reduction.

This study focuses on sodium restriction and weight reduction for hypertension control, not on reducing saturated fat intake (fails criterion 2). This study does target saturated fat reduction (achieved 10.3% decrease in % energy from saturated fat). However, duration is only 1 year (fails criterion 6 requiring minimum 24 months). Additionally, outcomes are limited to saturated fat intake, weight, and LDL cholesterol - there are no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes (fails criterion 7).

This is a weight control study using anorexiant medications, not a dietary intervention targeting saturated fat reduction (fails criterion 2). Outcomes are limited to lipoprotein subclasses with no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity data (fails criterion 7). Additionally, the intervention includes nutritional supplementation which may be considered multifactorial.

Outcomes are limited to plasma lipid concentrations with no mortality or cardiovascular morbidity data (fails criterion 7).

This is an observational study examining risk factors for insomnia, not a randomized intervention (fails criterion 1). The outcome is insomnia, not mortality or cardiovascular morbidity (fails criterion 7). There is no dietary intervention focused on saturated fat reduction.

This is a secondary analysis from the WHEL trial focusing on vasomotor symptoms in breast cancer survivors.
